key_insight: The classical 2-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm stabilizes in linear time, with a new upper bound of 5(n−1) rounds, improving the previous O(n log n) guarantee and nearly matching the Ω(n) lower bound.
engineering_relevance: This sharpens the practical runtime expectations for graph isomorphism and related graph-learning or combinatorial optimization pipelines that rely on Weisfeiler-Leman refinement.
method: Proves a tighter round-complexity bound for the classical 2-WL algorithm.
Extends the analysis to k-dimensional WL for every k ≥ 3.
Derives bounds via a broader class of tuple-coloring refinement sequences.
evidence_signal: The paper’s evidence is theoretical: it proves a new upper bound of 5(n−1) iterations for 2-WL and an improved O(n^{k−1}/(k−2)! + n^{k−2}) bound for k-WL.
watch_item: The result is about worst-case iteration counts, so actual speedups depend on graph structure and implementation details, especially for higher-dimensional WL where costs per round can be large.
paper_title: The Classical Weisfeiler-Leman Algorithm Stabilizes in $O(n)$ Rounds
